instruction: Remove the '>' indentation when replying to emails, and also change the reply position so your reply starts below the quoted message instead of above it.

Regex-based prefs.js parsing is correct; handles true/false/int/float/string types with appropriate default values (auto_quote defaults True when absent, reply_on_top defaults 1).
Sub-goal 2 check (reply_on_top == 0) correctly maps to 'reply starts below the quoted message instead of above it'.
Sub-goal 1 check (auto_quote == False) correctly maps to 'Remove the > indentation' as interpreted from the source trajectory — disabling auto-quoting removes all > prefixes.
Negative-control safe: initial state (auto_quote absent = True, reply_on_top = 1) yields score 0.0.
No incorrect expected parameter handling: metric does not call expected.get('rules') — it uses expected-independent hardcoded logic consistent with the rules dict.
Partial credit (0.5 per sub-goal) is semantically appropriate for this two-goal hardened task.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor semantic ambiguity: 'Remove the > indentation' could also be achieved by keeping auto_quote=true but changing the quoting style/format. The evaluator only accepts auto_quote=false, which is the most complete form of removal but is one specific implementation. Consider noting this in the instruction if strict quoting-disabled semantics are intended.

Logical tension: if auto_quote=false (quoting disabled), the reply_on_top setting is technically irrelevant since there is no quoted message. Both settings are valid Thunderbird configuration checks, but the instruction phrasing ('reply starts below the quoted message') presupposes quoting is enabled. Consider clarifying whether the intent is to disable quoting entirely or to keep quoting but remove the > character.
